# Instructions

Implement variable length quantity encoding and decoding.

The goal of this exercise is to implement [VLQ][vlq] encoding/decoding.

In short, the goal of this encoding is to encode integer values in a way that would save bytes.
Only the first 7 bits of each byte are significant (right-justified; sort of like an ASCII byte).
So, if you have a 32-bit value, you have to unpack it into a series of 7-bit bytes.
Of course, you will have a variable number of bytes depending upon your integer.
To indicate which is the last byte of the series, you leave bit #7 clear.
In all of the preceding bytes, you set bit #7.

So, if an integer is between `0-127`, it can be represented as one byte.
Although VLQ can deal with numbers of arbitrary sizes, for this exercise we will restrict ourselves to only numbers that fit in a 32-bit unsigned integer.
Here are examples of integers as 32-bit values, and the variable length quantities that they translate to:

```text
 NUMBER        VARIABLE QUANTITY
00000000              00
00000040              40
0000007F              7F
00000080             81 00
00002000             C0 00
00003FFF             FF 7F
00004000           81 80 00
00100000           C0 80 00
001FFFFF           FF FF 7F
00200000          81 80 80 00
08000000          C0 80 80 00
0FFFFFFF          FF FF FF 7F
```

[vlq]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variable-length_quantity

## Exception messages

Sometimes it is necessary to [raise an exception](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/errors.html#raising-exceptions). When you do this, you should always include a **meaningful error message** to indicate what the source of the error is. This makes your code more readable and helps significantly with debugging. For situations where you know that the error source will be a certain type, you can choose to raise one of the [built in error types](https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#base-classes), but should still include a meaningful message.

This particular exercise requires that you use the [raise statement](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/simple_stmts.html#the-raise-statement) to "throw" a `ValueError` if the sequence to decode or encode is incomplete. The tests will only pass if you both `raise` the `exception` and include a message with it.

To raise a `ValueError` with a message, write the message as an argument to the `exception` type:

```python
# if the sequence is incomplete
raise ValueError("incomplete sequence")
```

Use the instructions above to complete `variable_length_quantity.py`. Keep the existing function and class names: tests you cannot see import them. Use only the Python standard library.

{"content":"import unittest

from variable_length_quantity import decode, encode


class VariableLengthQuantityTests(unittest.TestCase):
    EXAMPLES = (
        (0x00000000, [0x00]),
        (0x00000040, [0x40]),
        (0x0000007F, [0x7F]),
        (0x00000080, [0x81, 0x00]),
        (0x00002000, [0xC0, 0x00]),
        (0x00003FFF, [0xFF, 0x7F]),
        (0x00004000, [0x81, 0x80, 0x00]),
        (0x00100000, [0xC0, 0x80, 0x00]),
        (0x001FFFFF, [0xFF, 0xFF, 0x7F]),
        (0x00200000, [0x81, 0x80, 0x80, 0x00]),
        (0x08000000, [0xC0, 0x80, 0x80, 0x00]),
        (0x0FFFFFFF, [0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x7F]),
        (0xFFFFFFFF, [0x8F, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x7F]),
    )

    def test_examples(self):
        for number, bytes_ in self.EXAMPLES:
            with self.subTest(number=number):
                self.assertEqual(encode([number]), bytes_)
                self.assertEqual(decode(bytes_), [number])

    def test_multiple_numbers(self):
        numbers = [number for number, _ in self.EXAMPLES]
        bytes_ = [byte for _, group in self.EXAMPLES for byte in group]
        self.assertEqual(encode(numbers), bytes_)
        self.assertEqual(decode(bytes_), numbers)

    def test_empty_sequences(self):
        self.assertEqual(encode([]), [])
        self.assertEqual(decode([]), [])

    def test_incomplete_sequences(self):
        for bytes_ in ([0x80], [0xFF], [0x81, 0x80], [0x00, 0x80]):
            with self.subTest(bytes_=bytes_):
                with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "^incomplete sequence$"):
                    decode(bytes_)

    def test_iterators(self):
        self.assertEqual(encode(iter([128, 0])), [0x81, 0x00, 0x00])
        self.assertEqual(decode(iter([0x81, 0x00, 0x00])), [128, 0])

    def test_redundant_leading_zero_group(self):
        self.assertEqual(decode([0x80, 0x00]), [0])

    def test_invalid_numbers(self):
        for number in (-1, 0x100000000):
            with self.subTest(number=number):
                with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "unsigned 32-bit"):
                    encode([number])

    def test_invalid_bytes(self):
        for byte in (-1, 256):
            with self.subTest(byte=byte):
                with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "between 0 and 255"):
                    decode([byte])

    def test_decode_overflow(self):
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "unsigned 32-bit"):
            decode([0x90, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x00])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
